title: Federated audit sink contracts & exactly-once forwarding for external SIEMs
creator: Amira Patel
description: Define and implement a hardened contract and runtime adapters for forwarding tenant-scoped audit events to third-party SIEMs (HTTP webhooks, Splunk HEC, Datadog intake, and syslog/Kafka bridges). Goal: provide measured end-to-end delivery guarantees (observable SLOs), preserve ordering where required, provide exactly-once semantics for classified security events, and ensure secure authentication (mTLS / signed JWT) for outbound connections.
slo: 99.95% successful delivery to configured external sinks within 24h, with p99 ack latency < 5s for synchronous forwards
implementation_notes: Approach: use at-least-once transport with per-event idempotency keys and monotonic sequence numbers per-tenant-sink to enable deduplication at the receiver. Where customers require stronger guarantees, negotiate exactly-once semantics by combining persistent per-sink offsets + DLQ reconciliation job. Outbound adapters must support mTLS or signed JWT, configurable batching window (100ms/1s), and backpressure signalling via TCP flow control or HTTP 429 semantics. Maintain a small in-memory resend buffer + durable WAL for crash recovery. Use tenant-scoped sequence namespace to avoid cross-tenant interleaving.

2025-03-11 — QA (Priya Shah): Added chaos tests for Bridge disconnect + duplicate deliveries. Found a dedup edge when WAL trimming coincides with reorder; tracking fix in ENG-15389.
2025-03-20 — Engineering lead (Ethan Brooks): Agreed to expose delivery metrics in Console and create alerting templates (sink_success_rate < 99.9% triggers pager).
